title: Finding the Actual Problem
excerpt: A simple loop to avoid building for the symptom, not the cause.
content: Most teams start with a request. That’s fine — it’s a clue, not a requirement.
A lightweight loop: trigger → current workaround → desired outcome → constraints. If a fix doesn’t improve the workaround or outcome, it’s likely solution-first.

title: Writing Crisper PRDs
excerpt: Structure, not length, makes a PRD useful.
content: Good PRDs reduce ambiguity for design and engineering. They clarify outcomes, guardrails, and edge cases.
Try: Problem, Goals/Non-goals, Users/Scenarios, Requirements, Open Questions, Metrics.
